Micron delivered another strong fiscal Q3, with record revenue, gross margin, and EPS — all exceeding the high end of our guidance. We guided to a record $50B quarter, as part of our FQ4 guidance. These results reflect the strength of our execution at a time when memory and storage have never been more important. As AI reshapes computing, memory and storage power performance, scale, and what is possible next. Our Strategic Customer Agreements are an important step forward in this new era. They accelerate the transformation of our business model, deepen long-term customer partnerships, and strengthen the predictability and durability with which we invest for the future. There is a lot of work ahead as we continue to build the capacity and advance the technology needed to support long-term AI growth. I want to thank our Micron team members for bringing their best to work every day. Your dedication is helping deliver the memory and storage the world needs for the AI era. Our progress builds on more than 47 years of hard work, tenacity, and innovation, with more than 61,000 patents representing the creativity of our inventors worldwide. Together, we accelerate intelligence to enrich life for all.

Today, we're proud to announce a strategic agreement with Anthropic that spans memory and storage AI architecture design, supply and demand, enterprise adoption of Claude across Micron and a strategic investment in Anthropic’s Series H funding round. As AI scales, getting the full stack right matters more than ever—and memory and storage play a central role in how efficiently models are trained, served and deployed. Together, we’re advancing how AI infrastructure is built, driving new levels of performance and scale for the workloads defining the AI era. It’s a strong example of how closer collaboration across the stack is accelerating what’s possible with AI. Learn more: https://bit.ly/4w7pcqY #AI #Innovation

I am thrilled to share that on May 30th, I had the incredible opportunity to present a Lightning Talk at the CURES Symposium! Since January, I have been working as an Undergraduate Student Researcher in the Vaske Lab at UC Santa Cruz, participating in a research immersion program focused on cancer genomics. It has been an incredibly rewarding experience to contribute to active pediatric cancer research while deepening my understanding of cancer biology. During my time in the lab, I’ve had the opportunity to: Identify genetic variants from short-read sequencing data in both DNA and RNA to support applications in precision medicine. Bridge the gap between computational and experimental approaches by validating these genetic variants using classical molecular biology techniques. Presenting our research at the CURES Symposium was a fantastic milestone. A huge thank you to Dr. Olena Vaske and the entire lab team for the continuous support, guidance, and for providing such a collaborative environment to grow as a scientist! Looking forward to continuing this important work in precision medicine.

I'm excited to share that I've graduated from the University of California, Santa Cruz with honors, earning a Bachelor of Arts in Global & Community Health and a minor in Theatre Arts. My time at UCSC allowed me to explore my passions for health, education, and community while gaining experiences that shaped both my personal and professional growth. From studying abroad in Denmark to working with children in a variety of educational settings, I've developed a deep appreciation for creating supportive and inclusive spaces where young people can learn and thrive. I'm also thrilled to announce that this August, I'll be moving to San Francisco and starting a full-time position at The Brandeis School of San Francisco as a Resident Kindergarten Teacher! I'm incredibly grateful for the mentors, professors, friends, family, and students who have supported me along the way, and I'm looking forward to this next chapter in education.

This week I got to visit NVIDIA’s headquarters in Santa Clara with my hackathon team. A few weeks ago, Justin Lee , George G. , and I competed in the NVIDIA x ASUS hackathon at UC Santa Cruz and won first place in the NVIDIA NemoClaw track with MonkeyClaw, our autonomous AI security system for testing agentic coding environments. Getting invited to NVIDIA HQ already felt surreal. But one moment from the visit stuck with me. Someone at NVIDIA asked what year we were. When I said we were freshmen, they were genuinely surprised. That was probably my favorite part of the whole experience. Not because being freshmen makes the project more impressive by itself, but because it reminded me that you do not need to wait until you feel fully ready to start building serious things. You can be early and still aim directly at the frontier. You can be new and still contribute. You can be a freshman and still put something in front of people operating at the highest level. And honestly, NVIDIA HQ felt like nerd heaven in the best way. The triangular architecture, the lights, the references to graphics and polygons, the campus lore, and casually walking past hardware that costs more than some houses made the place feel less like a normal office and more like a physical manifestation of the technology NVIDIA helped shape. Huge thank you to Nvidia for hosting the hackathon and inviting us out. Thank you to Justin and George for being such great teammates. And thank you to Ethan Einhorn , Zach L. , and Allison Ding for showing us around and making the visit so memorable. Leaving very grateful, and even more motivated to keep building at the intersection of AI systems, security, and hardware. #NVIDIA #AI #Cybersecurity #Hackathon #UCSC
